title: "Week 1 – Credibility and the three Rs"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-1-credibility-and-tools){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The term opens on the question that gives the course its name. Reproduction, robustness and replication are three different ways of repeating a study, and the three can return different verdicts on the same paper, as the four cases of the course show. The class meeting takes the talk from Part 1 of the deck of the housing-audit case, which is the deck of the first case of the term, and then starts the installation together, so that a machine that will not cooperate is found in the first week rather than in the third. The reading and the first modules are yours to finish before week 2.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 1 | In class. What social science is for; false positives and forking paths; the evidence from replications and many-analysts studies; incentives and questionable research practices; the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset; why 'replication' names three different operations; the practices of open research; the SCORE programme and its three studies, with the finding that their results do not travel together; Multi100 from the position of an analyst inside it; and the computational toolchain. | 75 minutes |
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd) | Begun in class, finished at home. Install R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace of the housing-audit case and run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until every line prints OK; the last check fits the reference specification and prints −19.97 percentage points. This is Task 1 of the first case. Open the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-1-setup) once as well, the fallback when a machine fails, and use the [help page](../../help.qmd) for the problems that others have met. | 60 minutes, once |
| [The opening page](../../index.qmd#cases), the four cases and [the five tasks](../../index.qmd#exercise) | Read the four case cards in the order of the term: the claim of each case, what it teaches, its data, and what reproduction, robustness and replication found on it. Then read the five tasks that every case repeats. | 20 minutes |
| [Resources – Glossary](../../resources.qmd#glossary) | Reproducibility, robustness and replicability defined side by side, with the other terms that the slides used. | 25 minutes |
| [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) | Section 1 and the section on the IDE that you chose, then the six steps of [section 6](../../companion/ide.qmd#sec-try) in the workspace that you have just installed, which use every pane that the tasks need. | 60 minutes |
| [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd), sections 1 to 5 | R and the IDE; the console, the script and the report; objects and vectors, and why the mean of a column of 0s and 1s is a share; data frames; installing and loading packages. | 60 minutes |

**By the end of the session** you have R, Quarto and an IDE installed, the workspace of the housing-audit case passing its setup check, and a paragraph in your own words that tells reproduction, robustness and replication apart and says what each of them found on one of the four cases.
